checks.reason: Apps must be registered for a Client ID/Client Secret and use OAuth2 server-side or client-side flows; username/password flow is described as a last resort.

The $0 Free plan lists 'API Integrations: 1000 calls per hour', and developers.podio.com/api-key says you just sign up and open the API key tab; no app review or install cap is documented (limits are per user per key, add-ons only raise rate).
Podio API is a JSON-over-HTTPS REST API called with an OAuth2 Authorization header.
Vendor (Progress) documentation says the Podio MCP Server is live at https://mcp.podio.com/mcp with OAuth; it is in beta.
Free self-serve keys with no review; only gate is rate limits (1,000 calls/hour per user per key), which does not block building or testing.
Clients are registered in the Zoho Developer Console to get Client ID/Secret; server-based apps are 'intended for use by multiple Zoho accounts'.
The credit table includes 'Free Edition | 5000 credits', so the API works on the free edition; client registration is self-serve with no review or install cap described.
Zoho CRM API v8 is a REST API metered by credits.
Zoho CRM developer docs: 'Zoho CRM provides these as pre-built MCP servers, so you don't need to build, host, or maintain any infrastructure.'
Self-serve OAuth client plus free-edition API credits allow building and testing today.
Admins generate API keys under Settings > Integrations > API Keys; OAuth client credentials are not self-serve, so a toolkit would use API keys.

OAuth apps can only be registered by contacting Copper ('To register your application, contact us' -> partners@copper.com), an approval gate for multi-tenant install; the Developer API is Professional/Business-tier only (support article 9623758) but every plan has a 14-day free trial, so per v2 precedence approval_required holds (would be paid_plan only if trials exclude the API, which docs do not say).
Copper Developer API is a REST/JSON API documented per resource (people, companies, opportunities, etc.).
Copper's page says an official MCP server is 'COMING SOON' with beta launching November 2026 but documents no endpoint; a marketing announcement alone counts as none_found.
'Developer API' is listed only for Professional (and Business) tiers and OAuth needs Copper registration, so buildable but gated.
Users enable and copy an API Key from their Profile; it is exchanged (with client ID) for a 15-minute token via OAuth2 client_credentials, so the end-user credential is an API key.

DealCloud offers only 'Schedule a demo' (no trial/self-serve signup); API capability must be enabled by a site admin or the customer's CSM per the API Keys doc, so credentials require being an enterprise customer.
REST endpoints under {baseUrl}/api/rest/v1/ with Bearer tokens.
Intapp's DealCloud API docs document the DealCloud MCP Server with OAuth 2.0 and .well-known discovery for Claude/ChatGPT/Copilot clients.
Buildable with a customer site's API key, but gated on being an enterprise customer with API capability enabled; the enum lists 'enterprise customer' as a caveat gate.
'The Pylon API uses Bearer authentication' with admin-created API tokens; no OAuth app option is documented for the REST API.
No free plan; plans are booked via demo/sales and 'Pylon offers free trials for prospects' set up by a sales rep, so credentials come only through sales.
Feature table lists 'REST API' and 'Webhooks' on Professional, Advanced and Enterprise.
Pylon docs document its hosted MCP server at https://mcp.usepylon.com (US) and https://mcp.eu.usepylon.com (EU).
Full REST API exists but testing requires a sales-provisioned trial or paid customer account.

'You need to create an OAuth2 application before you can use the API'; the Authorization Code flow 'is typically used for integrations to be used by other Help Scout users', with no review step described.

'The Free plan does not include access to the API or integrations'; API is on Standard/Plus/Pro, and the pricing FAQ gives a 15-day no-card trial of Standard/Plus with all plan features, so the free path to credentials is trial-only.
Inbox (Mailbox) API 2.0 is a REST API with per-plan rate limits (200/400/800 calls per minute).
Help Scout docs: 'Help Scout MCP gives AI assistants secure, official access', endpoint https://mcp.helpscout.net/mcp, on Standard/Plus/Pro.
Buildable via self-serve OAuth app, but API needs a paid tier after the 15-day trial (Free plan excluded).
API keys are for private apps only; OAuth2 is mandatory for public apps installed by other merchants.

Public apps must be submitted on the Developer Portal for Gorgias review (with a test account) before they are listed/installable; sandbox is a trial account converted by the partnerships team. Review outranks the trial gate under v2 precedence.
Gorgias exposes a REST API (tickets, customers, macros, etc.) authenticated by API key or OAuth2 bearer token.
Gorgias announces 'a first-party server' in open beta, included at no extra cost on any plan.
Buildable and testable via trial/sandbox, but public multi-tenant launch needs Gorgias app review.
'Each bot is given a unique authentication token' from BotFather, passed in the URL path https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/METHOD_NAME (a static key, not OAuth).
Anyone can create a bot via BotFather and get a token at no cost; no review or install cap is documented.
HTTP-based API over HTTPS supporting GET/POST with query, form or JSON parameters (RPC-style HTTP; rest is the closest enum value).
Telegram's Bot API docs make no mention of MCP, and searching turned up only community servers (sparfenyuk, chigwell, overpod, lexfrei), none on Telegram's domains.
Free, instant bot tokens and a documented HTTP API mean a toolkit can be built and tested today.
